clues: This city is hilly, which is rare in its flat southern state. It sits at the southern end of a red hills region.
Summers here are long and tropical, hotter than the beach towns to the south. Winters are short and mild, with barely a touch of cold.
The lawmakers were tired of long boat trips to two far ports. In 1824, they chose this old town site, halfway in between.
This city's name is a Muskogean word. It is often translated as "old fields" or "old town".
The governor of Florida works in this city. The state capitol tower rises here, near the top of one of its high hills.
